name: dual-frontier-governance-pulse
purpose: Track adverse and improvement evidence in parallel so governance can identify both unresolved problems and practices/outcomes worth learning from without netting one against the other.
hard_rules: never subtract improvement signals from adverse signals to create a net governance sentiment score
never treat activity or expenditure as outcome progress by itself
never infer that an intervention caused a positive outcome merely because both appear in the same report
never treat local improvement as proof that the broader domain problem is resolved
never treat absence from the pulse as proof that no adverse or improvement evidence exists
only treat a positive outcome as a learning candidate when it is at least corroborated and has an associated intervention or practice reference
transfer of a learning candidate to another jurisdiction or incident requires separate evidence and authority review

stress_frontier: What materially worsened or remained unresolved?
Which failures recur across place or time?
Which adverse states have the greatest humanitarian or system consequence?
progress_frontier: Where did the desired state measurably improve?
Which improvements are durable rather than momentary?
Which successful outcomes have enough intervention context to justify a learning hypothesis?
paired_learning: What differs between adverse and improvement cases in the same domain/topic?
Which difference is causal evidence versus merely contextual correlation?
What can be tested through replay or shadow operation before changing policy?

nocturnal_boundary: Nocturnal preserves sourced developments and longitudinal matter history. The governance control plane classifies public-good state direction under a domain constitution; Nocturnal should not be required to editorialize developments as good or bad.
success_boundary: A useful pulse improves problem selection, learning hypotheses and intervention review. It is not validated merely because it produces balanced-looking positive and negative lists.
